findings.reason: §6 must name nova/transport/coupled_window.py and window_batch.py as consumers to re-point onto solve.fixed_point / the new receipt adapter (as it does for the labeller) before fixed_point.py is deleted, or the retirement breaks coupled transport and its window batching.
findings.text: §6 retires fixed_point.py and shrinks forward.py to the request/receipt adapter, but nova/transport/coupled_window.py binds equilibrium.fixed_point.residual (:1658), imports ForwardEquilibrium/ForwardProfile from nova.equilibrium.forward (:43) and TopologyClass from nova.equilibrium.topology (:45), and nova/transport/window_batch.py also imports TopologyClass (:21); coupled_window.py additionally runs its own fixed-point driver (implicit_window_state with a fixed_point_map loop, :147-193) that is a second fixed-point owner beside solve.fixed_point; the plan records a consumer ruling re-pointing the batched labeller but names transport nowhere, and §6's import census is scoped to nova/equilibrium only, so the transport bindings would survive the deletion silently

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design is four pure functions (topology.read, current.book, gs.apply, solve.fixed_point), each hiding a whole subsystem (a connectivity-aware topology read, an exact-clip booking, the map plus its implicit Picard / moment-map / boundary-flux derivatives, and a Newton-GMRES solve) behind a single narrow call site, not a spread of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan adds solve.fixed_point as the fixed-point owner and §6 deletes fixed_point.py, but nova/transport/coupled_window.py already runs its own coupled fixed-point iteration and binds the module being deleted, and the plan names no transport consumer to re-point.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; each section that adds an entry point names what it retires or replaces in its own text (§3 clipped_support_current_moments, §4 the ForwardFluxOperator map, §5 newton_krylov/picard/operator_request_body, §6 the module deletion list), so no section adds surface without accounting for the removed surface.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites a specific mechanism or owner for every subsystem it adds, and each named target exists in the tree: topology.read extends contour_tree.build_contour_tree (nova/equilibrium/contour_tree.py:384) over contour_tree_mesh.build_contour_mesh (:193); current.book cites clip_quadrature.clipped_support_quadrature (:415), _quadratic_support_vertices (:852) and its JVP; gs.apply cites the operand-flattening machinery in forward_operator.py (_flatten_shared_flux_stencil :147, _SourceLayout :2122, _OperatorPytreeAux :2239); solve.fixed_point cites the single-site GMRES kernel in fixed_point.py (_single_site_krylov :2619, _krylov_machine :2216, _steepest_descent_promotion :1672); the row scale is bound to constraint.ConstraintPair (:237); the policy is carried by solve_request.ForwardSolvePolicy (:233); the null kernels are nova/biot/null.py and nova/biot/fieldnull.py.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every added module is stated as a replacement, not a parallel layer: §4 says "gs.apply replaces the map ForwardFluxOperator performs today rather than wrapping it"; §2 replaces Topology.read and read_with_connectivity in topology.py; §3 replaces clipped_support_current_moments; §5 replaces newton_krylov, picard and operator_request_body; §6 deletes the superseded files.
